title: Ranking metrics and calibration error

wrong.precision_divides_by_hits.py: precision_at_k divides by the number of results returned instead of k, rewarding short lists
wrong.recall_divides_by_k.py: recall_at_k divides by k instead of the number of relevant items, so it is just precision
wrong.mrr_uses_last_relevant.py: mrr scores the rank of the last relevant result instead of the first
wrong.ndcg_linear_gain.py: ndcg_at_k uses gain g instead of 2^g - 1, undervaluing highly relevant results
wrong.ndcg_ideal_from_top_k_only.py: ndcg_at_k builds the ideal ordering from only the retrieved top k, so missing better results is never punished
wrong.ndcg_all_zero_is_nan.py: ndcg_at_k divides by an ideal DCG of zero when nothing is relevant, giving NaN
wrong.ece_unweighted_bins.py: ece averages bin gaps equally instead of weighting by bin size
wrong.ece_signed_gap.py: ece lets over- and under-confident bins cancel instead of taking the absolute gap

hints: Precision@k and recall@k share a numerator, the relevant items in rel[:k]; they differ only in the denominator (k versus the corpus total). MRR needs np.flatnonzero(rel > 0) and the first index plus one.

DCG sums (2^g - 1) / log2(rank + 1) with rank starting at 1, which is np.log2(np.arange(2, n + 2)) for n items. The ideal is the same function on the whole list sorted descending, truncated at k. Divide only if the ideal is positive.
Bin index = min(floor(p * bins), bins - 1). For each non-empty bin add (count / n) * |mean(y) - mean(p)|. Weighting by count and taking the absolute value are both load-bearing.
